text: The $\textbf{'Black Summer'}$ bushfires of 2019-2020 burnt millions of acres primarily in the states of New South Wales and $\textbf{Victoria}$ in $\textbf{Australia}$.
explanation: The fires were among the most devastating in Australia's history, destroying thousands of homes and killing billions of animals.

text: In August 2020, a massive explosion occurred at the port of $\textbf{Beirut}$, the capital city of $\textbf{Lebanon}$, situated on the $\textbf{Mediterranean}$ coast.
explanation: The blast was caused by improperly stored ammonium nitrate and caused widespread destruction across the city.

text: The city of $\textbf{Wuhan}$, where the COVID-19 pandemic originated, is the capital of $\textbf{Hubei}$ province in central $\textbf{China}$.
explanation: Wuhan is a major transportation hub, often called the 'Chicago of China' due to its key role in domestic transit.

text: The $\textbf{Taal Volcano}$, which erupted in January 2020, is located on the island of $\textbf{Luzon}$ in the $\textbf{Philippines}$.
explanation: Taal is known for being a 'lake within a volcano within a lake' and is one of the country's most active volcanoes.

text: The $\textbf{United Kingdom}$ officially left the $\textbf{European Union}$ (Brexit) in 2020, changing the political geography of $\textbf{Europe}$.
explanation: The UK became the first and only sovereign country to have left the EU.

text: In 2020, $\textbf{Death Valley}$ in $\textbf{California}$ recorded a temperature of 54.4°C (129.9°F), one of the highest reliably recorded temperatures on $\textbf{Earth}$.
explanation: Death Valley is known as the hottest, driest, and lowest national park in the United States.

text: The $\textbf{Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam}$ (GERD) on the $\textbf{Blue Nile}$ was a source of major geopolitical tension in 2020 between Ethiopia, Sudan, and $\textbf{Egypt}$.
explanation: Egypt fears the dam will significantly reduce its water supply from the Nile, which is essential for its agriculture.

text: Massive swarms of $\textbf{Desert Locusts}$ devastated crops across $\textbf{East Africa}$ in 2020, affecting countries like Kenya, Somalia, and $\textbf{Ethiopia}$.
explanation: The infestation was the worst in decades, threatening food security in an already vulnerable region.

text: Hurricane $\textbf{Laura}$ made landfall in August 2020 as a Category 4 storm near Cameron, $\textbf{Louisiana}$, causing severe flooding.
explanation: The 2020 Atlantic hurricane season was the most active on record, exhausting the regular list of storm names.

text: The $\textbf{Esperanza Base}$ in $\textbf{Antarctica}$ recorded a new high temperature record of 18.3°C (64.9°F) in February 2020.
explanation: This record highlighted the rapid warming occurring on the Antarctic Peninsula.

text: The $\textbf{Pantanal}$, the world's largest tropical $\textbf{Wetland}$, suffered catastrophic fires in 2020, located mostly within $\textbf{Brazil}$.
explanation: Roughly a quarter of the entire biome burned, killing millions of animals.

text: The $\textbf{Aegean Sea}$ was the site of a powerful magnitude 7.0 earthquake in October 2020, affecting $\textbf{Turkey}$ and $\textbf{Greece}$.
explanation: The quake caused a mini-tsunami and significant damage in the city of Izmir.

text: The $\textbf{Norilsk Oil Spill}$ in May 2020 occurred in the $\textbf{Arctic Circle}$ region of $\textbf{Russia}$, releasing tonnes of diesel fuel into local rivers.
explanation: It was one of the worst oil spills in modern Russian history, linked to melting permafrost destabilizing a fuel tank.

text: The $\textbf{Nagorno-Karabakh}$ region was the subject of a war in 2020 between $\textbf{Armenia}$ and $\textbf{Azerbaijan}$.
explanation: The conflict resulted in significant territorial shifts in the South Caucasus region.

text: The $\textbf{Strait of Hormuz}$ lies between $\textbf{Iran}$ and the Musandam Peninsula of $\textbf{Oman}$ (and the UAE).
explanation: It is the only sea passage from the Persian Gulf to the open ocean.

text: The $\textbf{Mekong Delta}$ in $\textbf{Vietnam}$ faced a historic $\textbf{Drought}$ and saltwater intrusion in 2020, threatening global $\textbf{Rice}$ supplies.
explanation: The delta is known as the 'Rice Bowl' of Vietnam.

text: The $\textbf{Caspian Sea}$ is the world's largest inland body of water, classified as either a lake or a full-fledged $\textbf{Sea}$.
explanation: It lies between Europe and Asia and has characteristics of both sea and lake.

text: The $\textbf{Sierra Madre}$ is a major mountain range system in $\textbf{Mexico}$, consisting of the Occidental and Oriental ranges.
explanation: These ranges frame the Mexican Plateau.

text: The $\textbf{Ganges River}$ is the most sacred river to Hindus and is a lifeline to millions who live along its course in $\textbf{India}$ and $\textbf{Bangladesh}$.
explanation: It rises in the western Himalayas and empties into the Bay of Bengal.

text: The $\textbf{Danakil Depression}$ in $\textbf{Ethiopia}$ is one of the hottest and lowest places on Earth, known for its colorful hydrothermal $\textbf{Pools}$.
explanation: It is a geological depression resulting from the divergence of three tectonic plates.

text: The $\textbf{Suez Canal}$ connects the Mediterranean Sea to the $\textbf{Red Sea}$.
explanation: It creates a direct shipping route between Europe and Asia.

text: The $\textbf{Great Slave Lake}$ is the deepest lake in $\textbf{North America}$, located in the Northwest Territories of $\textbf{Canada}$.
explanation: It reaches depths of over 600 meters.

text: The $\textbf{Taklamakan Desert}$ is a desert in southwest Xinjiang in Northwest $\textbf{China}$, bounded by the Kunlun Mountains and the Pamir Mountains.
explanation: It is one of the world's largest shifting sand deserts.

text: The $\textbf{Hudson Bay}$ is a large body of saltwater in northeastern $\textbf{Canada}$, which drains a very large area of North America.
explanation: It is relatively shallow and is considered an epicontinental sea.

text: The $\textbf{Strait of Kerch}$ connects the $\textbf{Black Sea}$ to the $\textbf{Sea of Azov}$ and separates the Crimean Peninsula from Russia.
explanation: It is a strategic chokepoint heavily controlled by Russia since the annexation of Crimea.

text: The $\textbf{Lake Titicaca}$ is located on the border of $\textbf{Bolivia}$ and $\textbf{Peru}$ and is the highest navigable lake in the world.
explanation: It sits at 3,812 m (12,507 ft) above sea level in the Andes Mountains.

text: The $\textbf{Darrien Gap}$ is a break across the $\textbf{Pan-American Highway}$ consisting of a large watershed, forest, and mountains between $\textbf{Panama}$ and $\textbf{Colombia}$.
explanation: It is known for being extremely difficult and dangerous to cross.

text: The $\textbf{Zambezi River}$ is the fourth-longest river in Africa and flows into the $\textbf{Indian Ocean}$, famous for $\textbf{Victoria Falls}$.
explanation: Victoria Falls is located on the border between Zambia and Zimbabwe.

text: The $\textbf{Caucasus Mountains}$ lie at the intersection of Europe and Asia, stretching between the $\textbf{Black Sea}$ and the $\textbf{Caspian Sea}$.
explanation: They contain Mount Elbrus, the highest peak in Europe.

text: The $\textbf{Coral Sea}$ lies off the northeast coast of $\textbf{Australia}$ and contains the $\textbf{Great Barrier Reef}$.
explanation: It was the site of a major naval battle during WWII.

text: The $\textbf{Strait of Messina}$ separates the island of $\textbf{Sicily}$ from the $\textbf{Italian}$ mainland.
explanation: It connects the Tyrrhenian Sea with the Ionian Sea.

text: The $\textbf{Rio Grande}$ forms part of the border between the $\textbf{United States}$ and $\textbf{Mexico}$.
explanation: It flows from Colorado to the Gulf of Mexico.

text: The $\textbf{Loire River}$ is the longest river wholly in $\textbf{France}$, known for the many $\textbf{Châteaux}$ (castles) in its valley.
explanation: The Loire Valley is a UNESCO World Heritage site.

text: The $\textbf{Khyber Pass}$ is a mountain pass connecting $\textbf{Afghanistan}$ and $\textbf{Pakistan}$, historically an important trade route.
explanation: It cuts through the Spin Ghar mountains and was part of the Silk Road.

text: The $\textbf{Simpson Desert}$ is a large area of dry, red sandy plain and dunes in $\textbf{Central Australia}$.
explanation: It is famous for the Big Red sand dune.

text: The $\textbf{Sea of Japan}$ (East Sea) is a marginal sea between the Japanese archipelago, Sakhalin, the Korean Peninsula, and $\textbf{Russia}$.
explanation: It has almost no tides due to being nearly enclosed.

text: The $\textbf{Po River}$ is the longest river in $\textbf{Italy}$, flowing eastward across northern Italy into the $\textbf{Adriatic Sea}$.
explanation: The Po Valley is the industrial and agricultural heartland of Italy.

text: The $\textbf{Gulf of Tonkin}$ is located off the coast of northern $\textbf{Vietnam}$ and southern $\textbf{China}$.
explanation: It is an arm of the South China Sea.

text: The $\textbf{Murray River}$ forms part of the border between the Australian states of $\textbf{New South Wales}$ and $\textbf{Victoria}$.
explanation: It is Australia's longest river.

text: The $\textbf{Lake Ladoga}$ in $\textbf{Russia}$ is the largest lake located entirely in $\textbf{Europe}$.
explanation: It is located near Saint Petersburg.
